public_rationale: The factual parts of the claim check out. NVIDIA's 10-Q for the quarter ended April 26, 2026, the latest before the post, reported $30 billion in multi-year cloud service agreement commitments. CoreWeave's SEC filing shows a $6.3 billion order dated September 9, 2025. Under it, NVIDIA 'is obligated to purchase the residual unsold capacity through April 13, 2032.' The speaker's conclusion that this is an 'anti-demand signal' is hedged with 'suggesting', so it is treated as his interpretation and not scored. NVIDIA itself says the agreements mainly support its R&D, which is a different reading. The yearly amount of $6 billion or more through 2028 could not be checked against a readable copy of the filing.
limitations: The primary SEC filings could not be read directly, so the evidence is reports and summaries quoting them.
The '$6 billion or more a year through 2028' detail is unverified.
The hedged inference about unsold capacity is not assessed.

public_payload.normalized_proposition: NVIDIA's $30 billion in commitments to rent back its own GPUs is an anti-demand signal suggesting billions in unsold capacity.

statement.excerpt: Another concerning anti-demand signal is the fact that NVIDIA has committed to $30 billion in multi-year cloud compute agreements, spending $6 billion or more a year through 2028 to rent back its GPUs

from_speaker: NVIDIA has committed to $30 billion in multi-year cloud compute agreements
spending $6 billion or more a year through 2028
NVIDIA is 'obligated to purchase the residual unsold capacity' through April 2032
suggesting that there would be residual capacity that had gone unsold
our_interpretation: The facts he asserts are tested: about $30 billion in multi-year cloud service commitments, roughly $6 billion or more a year through 2028, and a $6.3 billion CoreWeave order under which NVIDIA must buy residual unsold capacity through April 2032.
'Anti-demand signal' and 'suggesting ... unsold' are his hedged reading of those facts. They are not scored as a claim that capacity actually went unsold.

Target period: NVIDIA's commitments as disclosed before the 2026-07-22 post. That covers the CoreWeave order signed 2025-09-09 through the latest 10-Q before the post, for the quarter ended 2026-04-26.
criteria.support_condition: NVIDIA or counterparty filings, or reliable reports of them, show about $30 billion in multi-year cloud service commitments, and a $6.3 billion CoreWeave order obliging NVIDIA to buy residual unsold capacity through April 2032.
criteria.contradiction_condition: The filings show materially different commitment totals, or show that the CoreWeave order has no residual-capacity purchase obligation or a materially different value or end date.
